w:r.w:t: This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) describes the functional and non-functional requirements for the Second-Hand Car Rental & Purchasing Platform. The system is a Java web-based application developed using Spring Boot, JSP Servlets, HTML/CSS, and Bootstrap. Data is stored using file read/write operations (text files) instead of a database, in compliance with the SE1020 project requirements.
The document serves as a reference for the development team, lecturers, and evaluators during the viva presentation.
The Second-Hand Car Rental & Purchasing Platform enables users to browse, rent, and purchase second-hand vehicles through a web interface. The system is composed of four core modules:
User Management - Handles registration, login, profile updates, and account deletion.
Vehicle Listing Management - Allows administrators/sellers to add, view, update, and remove vehicle listings.
Vehicle Purchase Management - Manages purchase requests, approvals, and purchase records.
Rental Booking Management - Handles rental bookings, availability checks, and booking cancellations.
Administrator - manages vehicles and platform settings
Registered customer who can rent or purchase vehicles
Plain text file used as data storage (.txt)
Java framework for building web applications
Backend: Java, Spring Boot, JSP Servlets
Data Storage: Text files (.txt) - users.txt, vehicles.txt, purchases.txt, rentals.txt

The platform is a web application where registered users can view second-hand car listings, book rentals, or purchase vehicles. Administrators manage vehicle listings and oversee all transactions. All data is persisted in plain text files using Java file I/O.
Unregistered visitor, can view listings only
Can rent/purchase vehicles and manage own profile
Manages vehicle listings and oversees all records
Instead of a database, the system uses the following text files for data persistence:
userId, name, email, password, role, phone
vehicleId, brand, model, year, price, type, status, ownerId
purchaseId, userId, vehicleId, date, amount, status
rentalId, userId, vehicleId, startDate, endDate, totalCost, status
Each record is stored on a new line using a pipe delimiter (|) for easy splitting. Example:
Manages user accounts for the platform including registration, login, profile updates, and deletion.
A new user fills in the registration form. The system validates all fields, assigns a unique userId, and writes the record to users.txt.
Input Fields: Full Name, Email, Password, Phone Number, Role (User/Admin)
Validation: Email uniqueness check by reading users.txt before saving
File Operation: Append new line to users.txt
OOP: User class with private fields and getters/setters (Encapsulation)
The system reads users.txt and displays all users in a table. Admin can search by userId or email.
File Operation: Read users.txt line by line, parse each record
Display: User List Page with search/filter functionality
OOP: FileHandler utility class for reading (Abstraction)
A user can update their profile (email, phone, password). The system rewrites users.txt with the updated record.
File Operation: Read all records, update matching userId, rewrite file
OOP: RegularUser and AdminUser inherit from User base class (Inheritance)
Admin can delete a user account. The system removes the user line from users.txt.
File Operation: Read all records, skip the deleted userId, rewrite file
Cascade: Also removes related rental/purchase records
User class with private fields (userId, name, email, password, role) accessed via public getters/setters
AdminUser and RegularUser extend the abstract User base class
authenticate() method overridden differently in AdminUser vs RegularUser
Abstract User class defines common structure; FileHandler abstracts file I/O logic
Handles the addition, display, update, and removal of second-hand car listings stored in vehicles.txt.
Admin adds a new vehicle with full details. The record is saved to vehicles.txt with a generated vehicleId.
Input Fields: Brand, Model, Year, Price, Mileage, Type (Sedan/SUV/Van), Status (Available/Sold/Rented)
File Operation: Append new record to vehicles.txt
OOP: Vehicle class hierarchy with Encapsulation
All users can view the vehicle listings. Users can search by brand, model, or type.
File Operation: Read vehicles.txt, parse and filter records
Display: Vehicle Listing Page with Bootstrap cards
Admin can edit vehicle details such as price, mileage, or status.
File Operation: Read all vehicles, update matching vehicleId, rewrite file
Admin can delete a vehicle listing that is no longer available.
File Operation: Read all records, skip deleted vehicleId, rewrite file
Vehicle class with private fields (vehicleId, brand, model, price, type, status)
Sedan, SUV, and Van classes extend the abstract Vehicle base class
getDescription() method returns different formatted output per vehicle subclass
Abstract Vehicle class defines common listing structure
Manages vehicle purchase requests, tracking the full purchase lifecycle from request to completion. Records are stored in purchases.txt.
A registered user selects a vehicle and submits a purchase request.
File Operation: Append new purchase record to purchases.txt with status=PENDING
Vehicle Status Update: Update vehicle status to PENDING in vehicles.txt
Users can view their own purchase history. Admins can view all purchases.
File Operation: Read purchases.txt, filter by userId for regular users
UI: Purchase History Page with status badges
Admin reviews a pending purchase and either approves or rejects it.
File Operation: Update purchase status in purchases.txt; update vehicle status to SOLD if approved
OOP: PurchaseTransaction class with status management
A user can cancel a PENDING purchase request before admin approval.
File Operation: Remove record from purchases.txt; revert vehicle status to AVAILABLE
PurchaseTransaction class encapsulates purchaseId, userId, vehicleId, amount, status
calculateFinalAmount() behaves differently for cash vs financed purchase
Abstract processPayment() method defined in PurchaseTransaction
Handles all vehicle rental bookings including creation, viewing, updating, and cancellation. Records stored in rentals.txt.
A registered user selects a vehicle, picks start and end dates, and confirms a rental booking.
Validation: Check vehicle is AVAILABLE by reading vehicles.txt and rentals.txt
File Operation: Append rental record to rentals.txt; update vehicle status to RENTED in vehicles.txt
Cost Calculation: Total cost = daily rate * number of days
Users can view their active and past rentals. Admin sees all bookings.
File Operation: Read rentals.txt, filter by userId for regular users
UI: My Rentals Page showing status, dates, and cost
Admin can mark a rental as COMPLETED when the car is returned. User can extend rental dates if the vehicle is still available.
File Operation: Read all rentals, update matching rentalId, rewrite rentals.txt
On return: Update vehicle status back to AVAILABLE in vehicles.txt
A user can cancel an ACTIVE booking. The vehicle is set back to AVAILABLE.
File Operation: Remove record from rentals.txt; update vehicle status to AVAILABLE
RentalBooking class encapsulates rentalId, userId, vehicleId, dates, totalCost, status
calculateCost() returns different rates for daily vs weekly rentals
Abstract RentalBooking class defines booking structure with abstract calculateCost()
System should load any page within 3 seconds under normal usage
UI must be responsive using Bootstrap 5, compatible with desktop and mobile browsers
File I/O operations must handle exceptions gracefully using try-catch blocks
Passwords must not be stored in plain text; basic input validation required on all forms
Code must follow OOP principles with clear class separation and comments
Runs on any OS with JDK 17+ and Apache Tomcat / Spring Boot embedded server
Follow these instructions to set up and run the project from scratch using VS Code or IntelliJ IDEA.
Download and install JDK 17 or 21 from https://adoptium.net
Download and install IntelliJ IDEA (Community or Ultimate) from https://www.jetbrains.com/idea/
Download and install Git from https://git-scm.com
(Optional) Install VS Code with the Extension Pack for Java for initial development
Step 2: Create the Spring Boot Project
Open your browser and go to https://start.spring.io
Add the following Dependencies: Spring Web, Spring Boot DevTools, Tomcat (provided)
Click GENERATE, download the ZIP, and extract it to your project folder
Step 3: Configure Project for JSP Support
Open the project in IntelliJ IDEA: File > Open > select the pom.xml > Open as Project
Add the following dependency to pom.xml inside <dependencies>:
In application.properties add: spring.mvc.view.prefix=/WEB-INF/views/ and spring.mvc.view.suffix=.jsp
Inside src/main/java/com/carsplatform/ create the following packages:
model/ - All entity classes (User, Vehicle, RentalBooking, PurchaseTransaction, etc.)
service/ - Business logic classes (UserService, VehicleService, etc.)
controller/ - Spring MVC Controllers or JSP Servlets
data/ - Text files: users.txt, vehicles.txt, purchases.txt, rentals.txt
Create a base FileHandler.java class with the following methods:
readAllLines(String filePath) - reads all records from a txt file
appendLine(String filePath, String record) - adds a new record
rewriteFile(String filePath, List<String> lines) - rewrites file after update/delete
findById(String filePath, String id) - finds a specific record by ID

Each model class should have: private fields, public getters/setters, a toFileString() method to format the record for file storage, and a static fromFileString() method to parse a line from the text file.
Create Service classes for each module that use FileHandler to perform CRUD operations. Example for UserService:
registerUser(User u) - validate email, call fileHandler.appendLine()
getAllUsers() - call fileHandler.readAllLines(), parse each line into User objects
updateUser(User u) - read all, replace matching record, rewrite file
deleteUser(String userId) - read all, skip matching userId, rewrite file

Step 10: Run and Test the Application
In IntelliJ IDEA, open the main application class (annotated with @SpringBootApplication)
Click the green Run button or press Shift+F10
Open browser and go to http://localhost:8080
Test each CRUD operation for all four modules
Verify text files (users.txt, vehicles.txt, etc.) are updated correctly after each operation
All 4 modules implement full CRUD. Minimum 3 operations per module as required.
Abstract base classes, subclass inheritance, method overriding for polymorphism, private fields with getters/setters.
Dedicated FileHandler classes for each module. All data stored in .txt files using Java I/O.
Minimum 3 UIs per module using Bootstrap 5, responsive design, and form validation.
Each member commits their assigned module with meaningful commit messages.
Each member explains their module's backend Java code, OOP concepts, and file handling.
This SRS + class diagrams for all 4 modules + GitHub commit history in final report.
To satisfy the Individual Contribution & GitHub Commit History criterion (10 marks), each team member must commit their own work with clear messages. Recommended commit message format:
"Add User model class with encapsulation", "Implement UserFileHandler for CRUD", "Add registration and login JSP pages"
"Add Vehicle abstract class and subclasses", "Implement VehicleService CRUD operations", "Add vehicle listing and edit JSP pages"
"Add PurchaseTransaction class hierarchy", "Implement PurchaseService with file handling", "Add purchase request and history pages"
"Add RentalBooking abstract class", "Implement RentalService with availability check", "Add rental booking and my rentals pages"
